Question: How will Earthworms 
provide nutrients to the soil for faster 
growth? How will LED lights speed up the 
root growth? 
 
 
 Team number: 12540 
 
 Team name: Demeter 
 
 Challenge: Plant the moon 
 
Date: 4/21/23

Background/Experimental Parameters: 
Independent variable #1: light vs no light 
The moon goes 327.5 hours (about 2 weeks) with sunlight and 327.5 hours (about 2 weeks) without 
sunlight. Since this happens, the plants would go without light for 327.5 hours (about 2 weeks). If the 
micro-green radishes go without light for a minimum of 48, they will die. Furthermore, by incorporating 
LED lights, micro-greens will survive in the dark hours on the moon. LED lights are the closest artificial 
lights to mimicking the natural light from the Sun. The lights will also provide 12% heat. The Moon has 
drastically changing temperatures through the day and night. The LED lights will also help with 
regulating the plants to a temperature they can survive in. Micro-green radish are tough plants that can 
survive many temperatures, but the LED lights will give them the extra push to survival. We chose to 
grow micro-greens because they work well with different light fixtures. These micro-greens also only 
take 10-12 days (about 1 week 5 days) to grow. They can very easily grow in the conventional growing 
 
Independent variable #2: earthworms vs no earthworms 
Earth worms will help provide nutrients into our lunar regolith and soil mixture. One of these nutrients is 
Nitrogen. Nitrogen isn’t found in lunar Regolith; Earth worms will leave castings of nitrogen in their 
tunnels. Earth worms will also eat the decaying matter and reproduce back into the mixture. Since the 
moon is dry, the worms will help improve water infiltration. Earth worms will help the roots expand 
through the soil by keeping the soil broken up. Without something in the soil feeding the micro-green 
radish nutrients they will not be able to grow. Earth worms are easy to take care of and they have survived 
in space before so we know that they can do this in space. The worms will even bring the Astronauts a 
sense of company. Space can be lonely for astronauts; the worms are a reliable pet or companion for the 
astronauts. This information allowed us to draw the conclusion that Earth Worms were the organism that 
we needed for this mission.

Experimental Contingency Plan: 
Students will participate in online Team meetings to discuss growth process and information. 
Team leaders will meet weekly at the grow lab (if possible) to collect measurements and take PH 
levels etc. with the coach. 
 
 
Hypothesis: 
We believe that the use of LED lights and Earth worms will speed up the process of growth of 
Micro-Green radish in a 50/50 mixture of soil and lunar regolith. This is because LED lights are 
proven to almost perfectly admit lights for plants that mimic the Sun. The Moon gets drastically 
changing amounts of sunlight. LED lights will help solve this issue. The LED lights will admit 
over 12% heat allowing the Micro-Greens to have an even admit of heat in space even in the 
drastic temperatures on the moon. The Earth worms have been brought to space before and 
survived. We know that the Earth worms will give the soil many benefits such as breaking up the 
soil to allow more root growth and water flow, giving the Micro- Greens nitrogen through their 
castings, and eating the decaying organic matter. The Earth worms will also give the astronauts 
company while in space. 
 
Experiment Design and Procedures: 
We are using Micro-Green Grow trays with natural sunlight until the Micro-Green Radishes 
sprout. The seeds will soak for 8-10 hours, and then will be misted lightly every day until they 
sprout. After the Micro-Greens sprout, we will place them in individual conventional gardening 
pots containing various amounts of Earth worms and a 50/50 mixture of lunar regolith and 
potting soil. We will place half of the pots under LED Lights and half with natural light. We will 
add varying amounts of Earth Worms and LED lights to different pots to see how much they 
affect the growth process. All pots will have the same watering process and schedule. We will 
keep track of the process by using a Data Notebook.
